name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19-year-old apprentice bricklayer and part-time student, Bamako, Mali
title: The Friday Tea Stop
situation: It's Friday evening and Aminata is walking home from the construction site. The air is cooling and the street is filling with people. She passes the tea vendor who sets up near the corner, where the sweet smell of ginger and mint drifts toward her. In her pocket she has the exact coins for a small cup, which she rarely allows herself. In her other pocket, she has the bus ticket she saved by walking to work this morning. The bus would get her home before dark, leaving her more time to study before her eyes burn out. She stops for a moment, looking at the vendor, then at the empty street stretching home.

context.relationship_profiles: The tea vendor is a familiar face she passes every Friday, but they have never exchanged more than a nod. Her younger sister in the village depends on her monthly remittances, which she sends through a money transfer service. Her master mason, Sékou, has taken to checking her arithmetic before approving her estimates, a sign of quiet trust.
context.tendencies: She has skipped the tea stop on at least four Fridays this month, each time pocketing the coins. She has walked to work every morning this week despite having bus fare saved, leaving the ticket unused. She has never taken the bus home on a Friday, preferring to save the ticket for a weekday when she is more tired.
context.current_state: Her shoulders ache from carrying cement bags, and her feet are blistered from the long day. She is thirsty but not desperately so, and the smell of tea is enticing. She is aware that darkness will fall in about forty minutes, and the walk home takes thirty.
context.immediate_memories: The scent of ginger and mint pulls her back to a memory of her mother brewing tea on a Friday evening after a long week at the market. The bus ticket in her pocket reminds her of the morning she chose to walk instead of using it, saving it for exactly this moment.
context.reflective_memories: She remembers the time she bought a small cup of tea and then had to borrow from her emergency fund when a bus fare increased unexpectedly. She recalls the year her mother walked two hours each way to save transport money, only to lose the stall anyway.
